fields.description: SAR_FILED: a SAR went to TRACFIN; every account of the customer stays frozen until TRACFIN answers (recorded on the SAR).
TRIGGER: the transaction that fired the rule. CONTEXT: the ones around it. REPORTED: pointed out by the customer.
The call to the customer on the number on file. CONFIRMED: they made the payment or the login. DENIED: they did not. NOT_REACHED: no answer.

Why a cleared alert was closed. FALSE_POSITIVE: the rule fired but nothing unusual happened: the customer confirmed the payment, or the pattern is everyday banking (salary in, rent out, money between their own accounts). EXPLAINED_BY_PROFILE: the activity was unusual for this customer, but a documented life event or income consistent with the profile explains it (a bonus, a car sale, a house move; payslip, deed or invoice on file). DUPLICATE: the same activity is already covered by another alert. ALREADY_INVESTIGATED: an open or recent investigation covers it. VERIFIED_WITH_COUNTERPARTY: confirmed with the other bank or the merchant.
When the alert must be decided. Card fraud (unusual card spend, card testing): within 24 hours. The others from their severity: critical 24 hours, high 3 days, medium 7 days, low 14 days.
RULE: raised by a monitoring rule. MANUAL: raised by an operator (a customer report, a doubt).

OPEN: new, in the AML or fraud queue. IN_REVIEW: an analyst works on it. SECOND_LOOK: handed to a senior analyst, out of the queues until they decide. CLEARED: closed, nothing suspicious. ESCALATED: sent to an investigation.
People only: the solde bancaire insaisissable, the RSA for one person, always left on the account.

RECEIVED: to handle. IN_PROGRESS: accounts and balances being checked. FUNDS_HELD: the amount is blocked (a hold); a seizure is paid once the debtor’s month to contest has passed. ANSWERED: the bank replied (nothing to hold, or an information request). PAID_OUT: the money went to the creditor or the Treasury. CLOSED: nothing left to do.

SEIZURE: a bailiff (commissaire de justice) seizes money for a creditor (saisie-attribution). PRECAUTIONARY_FREEZE: money blocked before a judgment (saisie conservatoire). TAX_GARNISHMENT: the tax office takes what is owed (SATD). INFORMATION_REQUEST: police or Tracfin ask what the bank knows; no money moves.
NEW: detected, to triage. REVIEW_OPENED: a KYB event review is open (its KYC case). DISMISSED: no review needed, with the reason.
AUTHORIZED: amount set aside. CLEARED: the merchant confirmed the final amount, booked on the account. SETTLED: the money moved between the banks through the card network.
A purchase at a shop or online, or cash taken out at an ATM.
The file sent to the card network (a generated specimen in this demo).
The next deadline on an open case: to file (120 days), for the merchant to answer, or to go to pre-arbitration (Visa 30 days, Mastercard 45). Empty once the case is closed.
CUSTOMER_REQUEST: from the customer’s dispute request (app or support ticket). FRAUD_DETECTION: the bank found the fraud itself (for example a tested card).

The card network’s rounds, in order. INITIATED: we are preparing the file. WAITING_CARDHOLDER: questions sent to the cardholder, out of the work queue until they answer. PRESENTED: filed with Visa or Mastercard; the merchant’s bank has 30 days to answer (Mastercard 45). REPRESENTED: the merchant contested with evidence; we have the same time to push back. PRE_ARBITRATION: we pushed back, last round before the network decides. ARBITRATION: the network decides (fee to the loser). WON: the customer is credited the amount (an unauthorised payment was refunded already), whether the merchant contested or not (the dates show which). LOST: the merchant proved its case; nothing is credited, and an unauthorised payment’s refund stays with the customer, the loss being the bank’s. WITHDRAWN: the customer dropped the claim (the order finally arrived), or the bank refunded and dropped it.

REQUESTED: to review. APPROVED: accepted, notice to send when one is due. NOTICE_SENT: a person closed by the bank gets two months’ notice (none for fraud or financial crime, none when the customer asks). PENDING_PAYOUT: waiting to send the remaining balance (the customer’s IBAN, the notary’s or the liquidator’s). CLOSED: balance sent, accounts closed. CANCELLED: the customer stayed.
PAID: the arrears were paid. PAYMENT_PLAN: a plan was agreed. RESTRUCTURED: the loan was spread over a longer term. WRITTEN_OFF: given up.
EARLY: under 30 days past due (reminders, calls). LATE: 30 to 89 days (formal notice). LEGAL: 90 days or more (court or a collection agency). WRITTEN_OFF: given up.
Where the customer took it after our answer. BANKING_MEDIATOR: free, gives an opinion within 90 days. ACPR: the banking supervisor, which collects complaints but does not settle them. COURT.
The mediator’s or the court’s opinion: for the customer, for the bank, or split.
Payment services: 15 business days to answer. Anything else: two months.
The partner app the customer came through (Lagoon...), empty for the bank’s own customers. A partner team’s scope (partner = Lagoon) shows it only its own customers.

PROSPECT: known, not a customer (never applied, or stopped answering). DECLINED: refused at onboarding, no account. ONBOARDING: application in progress. ACTIVE: a customer. SUSPENDED: accounts frozen pending a decision. OFFBOARDED: the relationship ended.

NOTIFIED: the death was reported, to handle. ACCOUNTS_FROZEN: the deceased’s own accounts stop (a joint account carries on with the survivor). CERTIFICATE_VERIFIED: the death certificate is checked. FUNDS_RELEASED: the balance went to the notary for the estate. CLOSED: done.

When the reasons for refusing the refund were sent to the Banque de France: the law allows the refusal only when the bank suspects the customer’s own fraud (art. L133-18 of the Monetary and Financial Code).
customer: filed in the app or on the website. An email: the support agent who logged it from a phone call or an email (support_ticket_ref).

fields.displayName: Eligibility · Refund by the next business day (PSD2)

fields.description: The kind of payment disputed; its detail (card payment, direct debit, transfer) is linked.

CHARGEBACK: claim filed with the card network. SEPA_DISPUTE: refund or recall through the SEPA rules. BANK_REFUND: unauthorised payment refunded by the bank, which bears the loss (no chargeback right after 3-D Secure, chip or contactless). CONTACT_MERCHANT: the customer must contact the merchant first. DECLINED: no grounds.

NEW: to review. WAITING_CUSTOMER: details asked from the customer. UNDER_INVESTIGATION: an unauthorised claim the bank doubts; refund refused for now, reasons sent to the Banque de France. ROUTED: sent to the card disputes desk (chargeback) or the payments desk (SEPA dispute). CLOSED: refunded, settled, declined, or the customer was asked to contact the merchant.

DISPUTED: the payment the case is about. PROVISIONAL_CREDIT: an unauthorised payment refunded by the next business day (PSD2) while its chargeback runs; the other chargebacks get no credit before they are won. CREDIT_REVERSAL: that credit taken back. REFUND: money given back to our customer (a chargeback won, a bank refund). RETURN: money sent back to the other bank. COMPENSATION: goodwill after a complaint.
The document as the customer sent it (a generated specimen in this demo).
The partner app the customer came through (Lagoon...), empty for the bank’s own customers. A partner team’s scope (partner = Lagoon) shows it only its own documents.
The approved platform this company chose instead of ours.
OUR_PLATFORM: we carry its e-invoices. OTHER_PLATFORM: it chose another approved platform; we only bank it.
Where other platforms send this company’s e-invoices, as published in the national directory.
Every company receives e-invoices since 2026-09-01; SMEs and micro-companies must send them from 2027-09-01.
Already sends its invoices as e-invoices, ahead of the deadline (since voluntary_since).
Transactions: 10 days after the period. Payments: the 10th of the next month (monthly VAT regime). SMEs must report from 2027-09-01: these companies report voluntarily, having started early.

TRANSACTIONS: sales with no e-invoice (to consumers, abroad), every 10 days. PAYMENTS: cash received on services sold to consumers or abroad, every month (B2B e-invoices report theirs with the CASHED status).
PENDING_SIGNATURE: the guarantor has not signed yet. ACTIVE: in force. CALLED: the loan defaulted and the guarantor is asked to pay. RELEASED: the loan was repaid. EXPIRED: past its end date.

PERSONAL_GUARANTEE: a person (often the director, or a parent) commits to pay. STATE_GUARANTEE: Bpifrance guarantees part of a business loan (no guarantor row). CASH_DEPOSIT: money blocked as security. PROPERTY / VEHICLE: an asset pledged.

Why the money is blocked. AUTHORITY_REQUEST: a seizure or a tax garnishment. FRAUD: money another bank recalls as fraud, held until we answer. INVESTIGATION: an open money-laundering investigation. SANCTIONS: an asset freeze. DISPUTE: a payment sent by mistake, held until our customer agrees to return it. INSOLVENCY: a court proceeding.
The case this request serves; its link is set on the request.

OPENED: the bank learned of the judgment. ACCOUNTS_FROZEN: the balance is held for the practitioner. CLAIM_FILED: the bank declared what it is owed, before the deadline. BALANCE_HANDED_OVER: the balance went to the liquidator. CLOSED: nothing left for the bank to do.

SAFEGUARD, RECEIVERSHIP (redressement), LIQUIDATION: court proceedings on a company. PERSONAL_DEBT_RESTRUCTURING: over-indebtedness of a person (surendettement), handled by the Banque de France commission.
AUTO_MATCHED: reference and amount agree. SUGGESTED: close but not certain (a typo in the reference, a partial payment), to confirm. CONFIRMED or DISMISSED by someone.
A readable rendering of the invoice (a generated specimen in this demo). A Factur-X invoice is this PDF with its data inside; UBL and CII invoices are data only, shown here as a PDF.

Received invoices only. KNOWN: the IBAN we already pay this supplier to. NEW_SUPPLIER: first invoice from it. CHANGED: another IBAN than the known one, checked before paying (a classic fake-invoice fraud).

The life cycle the tax office expects. SUBMITTED: deposited on the platform. REJECTED: non-compliant, to fix and send again. ISSUED / RECEIVED: on its way, then at the buyer’s platform. APPROVED: the buyer accepts it. DISPUTED: the buyer contests part of it. REFUSED: the buyer will not process it. PAYMENT_SENT: the buyer paid. CASHED: the seller received the money (mandatory for services when VAT is due on payment).
Services only: the seller pays VAT when it invoices, not when it is paid.
The partner app the customer came through (Lagoon...), empty for the bank’s own customers. A partner team’s scope (partner = Lagoon) shows it only its own cases.

Why a case was closed without approval. IDENTITY_FAILED: the selfie is not the ID holder. DOCUMENT_FORGED: an altered paper. SYNTHETIC_IDENTITY: a made-up identity. UBO_MISMATCH: owners unlike the RBE register. RISK_APPETITE: outside what the bank accepts. NO_RESPONSE: closed, the applicant stopped answering (not a refusal).

fields.displayName: Robot · Why it went to a person

fields.description: OPEN: new, in the onboarding queue. IN_REVIEW: an operator works on it. WAITING_CUSTOMER: documents asked from the client, out of the queue until they answer. PENDING_APPROVAL: waiting for a senior’s sign-off. ESCALATED: parked until the screening team decides on a hit. APPROVED / REJECTED: decided.
Card and transfer raises last until this date; an overdraft raise stays.
OVERDRAFT: the account can go below zero up to this limit (the only credit). CARD_PAYMENT / CARD_WITHDRAWAL: the card’s monthly payments or weekly withdrawals. TRANSFER: the largest transfer allowed.
The Banque de France FICP file (repayment incidents), checked before any consumer credit, as the law requires. NOT_CHECKED: business loans (the FICP covers individuals) or not studied yet.
Monthly charges plus this loan’s instalment, as a share of monthly income. Our limit is 35%.
Score from the analysis of the account’s history, out of 1,000.
The APR (TAEG in France): rate plus fees, mandatory on every consumer credit offer. 0 for a free pay-in-3.

SUBMITTED: just in. IN_REVIEW: the credit team studies it. WAITING_DOCUMENTS: payslips (a person) or the latest accounts (a company) asked. OFFER_MADE: an offer is out, waiting for the customer (and the guarantor). APPROVED: the offer was accepted; the loan is signed a few days later. DECLINED: refused, with the reason. WITHDRAWN: the customer never signed the offer.
Days since the oldest instalment still unpaid.
CURRENT: paid on time. LATE: an instalment is missed (1 to 89 days). DEFAULT: 90 days or more. RESTRUCTURED: the arrears were spread over a longer term. REPAID: nothing left to pay.
Consumer credit: the borrower can withdraw for 14 days after signing; the money is paid out no earlier than 7 days after signing. Empty for business loans.
The call back before deciding, on the number on file. CONFIRMED: the customer made the transfer. DENIED: they did not (rejected, the fraud team takes over). NOT_REACHED: no answer.
RANDOM: drawn at random. HIGH_RISK: a high-risk customer or an investigation, always sampled more. NEW_OPERATOR: the operator joined recently.
SCHEDULED: not due yet. PAID: taken from the account (the transaction). MISSED: the money was not there. PARTIAL: part of it was taken.
DRAFT: with the MLRO. SUBMITTED, ACKNOWLEDGED: filed with TRACFIN, waiting for its answer; the accounts stay frozen. ANSWERED: TRACFIN said what to do (tracfin_answer).
RELEASE_ACCOUNTS: the accounts open again. KEEP_BLOCKED: kept frozen for a judicial seizure or the prosecutor. EXIT_RELATIONSHIP: released and closed by the closure team.

fields.displayName: Hit · Date of birth on the list

fields.description: SANCTIONS: blocks until cleared. PEP: politically exposed person, leads to enhanced due diligence.
WE_ASKED: our customer wants money back from another bank. WE_ARE_ASKED: another bank wants money back from our customer.

OPEN: our turn to answer (in "Recalls we received"). WAITING_CUSTOMER: our customer was asked for their consent, out of the queue until they answer. WAITING_OTHER_BANK: we asked another bank. ACCEPTED / PARTIAL: money sent back, all or part. REFUSED: refused with a SEPA reason code.
REFUND: a direct debit paid back. RETURN: a debit we send back. RECALL: duplicate, technical or fraud. REQUEST_FOR_RECALL: a customer’s mistake (wrong IBAN or amount).
What the line is for, as on the customer’s statement. REFUNDS: money back after a dispute or a complaint (provisional credits, refunds, returns, goodwill). FEES: the bank’s charges.
How the money moved: card, SEPA transfer, direct debit, Wero, wallet to wallet, a fee, or an internal entry.

PENDING: authorised, not final yet. HELD: stopped by screening or fraud checks, waiting for a decision. BOOKED: on the account, final (the term of ISO 20022 and PSD2). REVERSED: cancelled. REJECTED: never went through.

🏠 Welcome, {{currentUser.firstName}}. This is the bank’s back office.

This demo bank runs its operations in Forest: its teams onboard customers, clear fraud and money-laundering alerts, investigate suspicions and settle disputes. The data is made up and stays on your computer, so try anything.
New here? Start with path ①: it takes three minutes.
Six paths, from the quickest to the deepest. Each page they open has a guide on its right.
① Work a case, like an operator
Take the next KYC case and follow its guided review: Forest shows the documents, AI runs the checks, you approve or ask for more. Each button answers with a result card.
How: Click Start processing on a queue, then ▶ Retail onboarding.
Shows: inboxes, workflows with AI steps, Smart Actions.
② Watch Forest work on its own
New applications go to a robot within a minute: it checks the ID and screens the person. Clean files are approved on their own, the others wait for a person.
How: Click ▶ Demo: send applications at the top of the desk, then watch its first two lists.
Shows: automated workflows, with a person for what is unclear.
③ Follow a suspicion across three teams
An analyst escalates an AML alert: it becomes an investigation. The investigator proposes a SAR: the MLRO files it with TRACFIN and the accounts are frozen.
How: Escalate an alert, then File a SAR on the Investigations desk, then sign it off.
Shows: work handed from one team’s inbox to the next.
④ Run the bank as a manager
Every queue of every team on one page: what waits now, what came in and went out each week, and where the backlog grows.
How: Read the tiles, then the weekly charts below them.
Shows: counters on saved filters, charts computed by your agent.
⑤ Make a page your own
Every page here was assembled without code. Move a tile, add a chart or a button, or start a blank page. Changes stay a draft for your team until you publish them.
How: Turn on the Layout Editor in the top bar, or + Add New in the left panel, then Workspace.
Shows: workspaces and the layout editor.
⑥ Learn it feature by feature
One page per Forest feature: what it does, where to see it in this bank, and how to set it up on your own data.
How: The full list is at the bottom of this page.
Shows: everything above, one piece at a time.
Each team works its queues on its own page. Open one to take a case.
Retail and business KYC: check the ID, the owners and the documents, then approve or ask for more.
AML and fraud alerts raised by the rules: clear the noise, escalate the real ones.
Open cases and screening hits: build the case file, ask for due diligence, draft the SAR.
The MLRO signs off: file the SAR, send it back to the analyst, or close without one.
High-value transfers to validate, and the SEPA recalls other banks send us.
Card and SEPA disputes: route each request, file chargebacks, answer the merchant’s bank.
Every queue of every team on one page: the manager’s view.
Short pages: what the feature does, where to see it in this bank, how to set it up.
Every table of your bank, browsable, with a page per customer that tells the story.
Saved lists your whole team shares: “transfers to validate” is one click away.
Each analyst gets the next task, in the right order, and nobody works the same case twice.
Your procedure, step by step on screen: the analyst follows it, and the hard cases go up.
Your business operations as buttons: a form, your code runs, a card shows what it did.
Live counters and graphs on your data, where the team works, with no BI project.
A page per team: its queue, the case, and the buttons to act, without a line of code.
When the built-in blocks are not enough, drop your own HTML, code and style into a page.
Analysts see what they need and do what they may; the MLRO signs, the rest cannot.
Your data never leaves your infrastructure: Forest sees the shape of your tables, not the rows.
AI that decides inside your procedure, explains why, and stays inside your permissions.
Who did what, on which record, and when: every click an auditor will ask about.
Forest’s servers keep the pages and settings. The records go from your agent, on your computer, straight to your browser.
Customers, documents and payments are made up for this demo bank. Try every button.
Each desk is built with Forest’s own components; its · hybrid version adds custom ones.

Hey again {{currentUser.firstName}}, and welcome to the Retail Onboarding workspace !
 
Here we will learn about the functional process of an onboarding and try and apply it on a couple of cases through Forest features !
First let's look at the functional process !
If you need to, you can reset the demo cases with this button 👉

1️⃣ First we check the file of the client (are all docs here?)
If not we request the missing docs from the client
2️⃣ Then we verify the ID documents via an OCR (are docs valid?) 
If not valid, we request new documents
3️⃣ We screen against AML/Sanctions lists (is the customer flagged?)
If they are, we park the case for reviewal by the screening team
4️⃣ We rate the risk following the suggestion given by the system
5️⃣ If it's low we onboard, if it's medium or high we escalate to senior officer !
6️⃣ That's it !

An inbox turns a segment into a queue. An analyst clicks “Next ticket” and gets the next case, sorted the way the team decided: oldest first, highest score first.

The task is theirs until they finish it. A cap stops anyone hoarding cases, and an idle task goes back to the queue on its own.

Let's try it out, follow the instructions on the right section below  👇
